summary: US stocks closed mixed on Election Day (Nasdaq +0.8%, Dow -0.4%) as chips rebounded; midterm results are still being counted, so the next 24h carry binary political risk. Oil's war premium is deflating on US-Iran talk hopes while Fed hike odds keep yields near 4.9% and gold weak.
events_next_24h: Wed all day USD US midterm election results (House/Senate control)
Thu 00:15 USD ADP employment (expected; FF calendar unavailable)
Thu 02:00 USD ISM services PMI (expected; FF calendar unavailable)
tier1_next_14d: CPI (Oct) · date unconfirmed (calendar dataset unreadable), expected mid-Nov

ES.why: S&P rose 0.4% as chips rebounded, but US midterm results land today and could swing it either way; funds sit mid-range.
ES.risk: A clear, market-friendly election result with stocks holding gains.

NQ.why: Nasdaq +0.8% on an AI/chip rebound, but funds are crowded long (94th pct) and election results are still pending.
NQ.risk: Tech extends higher after results; or a contested count triggers a crowded-long unwind.

YM.why: Dow fell 0.4% while tech led; no clear macro edge with midterm results still being counted.
YM.risk: Election outcome that clearly favours or hurts cyclicals.

RTY.why: Small caps are rate-sensitive and 10y yields near 4.9% plus Fed hike talk weigh, but the election could change fiscal outlook.
RTY.risk: A sharp move in yields after the election results.

NKD.why: Nikkei has been drifting lower around 63,000 with Tokyo shut for a holiday; US tech strength helps but election risk caps conviction.
NKD.risk: A weaker yen and US tech rally after results would lift it.

6E.why: Euro stuck near 1.12 with no fresh euro-area driver; the dollar's next move hinges on the election and Friday payrolls.
6E.risk: A decisive dollar move on election results.

6J.why: USD/JPY near 158 on wide rate gaps, but Tokyo's intervention zone and a likely December BoJ hike limit downside for the yen.
6J.risk: A break above 158 with no official pushback, or intervention-style yen spike.

6B.why: A BoE hike on Thursday looks almost fully priced, so the pound has little fresh fuel either way before the decision.
6B.risk: A dovish split vote or surprise hold at the BoE.

6A.why: The RBA hiked 25bp but three of nine members wanted a hold, so markets read it as a dovish hike and the Aussie fell toward 0.697.
6A.risk: AUD reclaims 0.70 on strong risk appetite.

ZN.why: 10y yields near 4.9%: a strong ISM lifted Fed hike odds, but the oil slump eased inflation fears; election and payrolls loom.
ZN.risk: A fiscal-heavy election result pushing yields higher.

GC.why: Gold sits below $4,000 near its annual low as rising Fed hike odds and high yields weigh; funds lean short but are not crowded.
GC.risk: Gold reclaims $4,000 or a contested election drives haven buying.

CL.why: Crude fell over 7% Monday on US-Iran talk hopes then rebounded near $98 on a reported Qeshm clash; funds already cut longs hard.
CL.risk: Formal Iran deal (down) or new Gulf clashes (up).
